title: Pierce County Sheriff’s Office deactivates its automated license plate readers
summary: The Pierce County Sheriff's Office deactivated its Flock ALPR system in response to Washington's newly signed Driver Privacy Act, which restricts ALPR use near schools, hospitals, and other protected areas, with violations classified as gross misdemeanors. The Sheriff's Office said it lacks technology to ensure compliance and cited concerns about ICE-related use driving the legislation.

key_quotes.quote: The Pierce County Sheriff's Office says it has deactivated its Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) system, commonly known as Flock cameras.

At this time, there is no available technology or operational capability that allows the Sheriff's Office to ensure that ALPR cameras can reliably differentiate between restricted and permitted locations in real time.
